brief.headline: Push for ₹0.35/NOS on the measuring-cup SKU to close the ₹82500 annual gap, then trade faster payment (30-day) for an across-the-board price cut.

priceAsk.summary: Target ₹0.35/NOS on the MESU. CUP 30MM TRANS.PP 2.5/5/10ML SKU, matching Premier Plastic's price.
priceAsk.basis: We pay Mars ₹0.38/NOS — an 8.6% premium over the ₹0.35/NOS we pay Premier Plastic for the same item. The open-market typical price for a 28 mm PP cap is ₹0.85–0.95/pc, with headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume, so ₹0.35 for a smaller measuring cup is market-fair and we already achieve it elsewhere.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to move from 45-day to 30-day payment in return for a price cut on all items.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days faster costs us ₹5.10 L in cash (₹10.19 L freed if we went to 30-day from zero, so the step from 45 to 30 is ₹5.10 L). Trade that for a price reduction worth at least the same.

brief.financialLeverage: Mars Plastics publishes no financials, so we can't gauge their cash position or how much our ₹1.24 Cr annual spend matters to them. Without that visibility, we lean on the price evidence we do have: Premier Plastic delivers the same SKU 8.6% cheaper, and the open market shows modest headroom below typical PP cap prices. We also have five strong alternate converters lined up (Manjushree, Mold-Tek, Hitech, Pearl, Pravesha), so Mars knows a second source is in play. Push firmly on price and payment, but don't squeeze so hard that a smaller private supplier walks — we need the gap closed and a backup qualified in parallel.

evidence.point: We overpay Mars by 8.6% on the measuring-cup SKU versus what we pay Premier Plastic.
The open-market typical price for a similar 28 mm PP cap is ₹0.85–0.95/pc, with headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume, so our ₹0.35 target is well below market and justified.
evidence.figure: askBand ₹0.55–1.20/pc; typical ₹0.85–0.95/pc; headroom to ₹0.65–0.80; verdict MARKET-FAIR

evidence.point: Moving payment from 45-day to 30-day ties up ₹5.10 L of our cash — we can trade that for a price cut.
Mars is private and publishes no financials, so we can't assess their health or how big a customer we are to them.
We spend ₹1.24 Cr annually with Mars on rigid plastic packaging.

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health B 65/100) — pharma bottles, caps, preforms; top second-source candidate already on our radar for packaging.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader for pails, containers, pharma — strong and profitable; a robust alternate for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Hitech Corporation Ltd
alternates.why: Listed converter with broad capability across moulded and blow-moulded bottles and caps — direct overlap with Mars's scope.

risks: Mars publishes no financials — we're flying blind on their cash health and whether they can afford to hold the line or might need our volume.
Our ₹1.24 Cr spend is modest; if Mars has bigger pharma customers, they may not budge much on price.
Pushing too hard without a qualified backup in place could leave us scrambling if Mars walks — qualify Manjushree or Mold-Tek in parallel before the final squeeze.
The ₹82500 annual excess is concentrated in one SKU (the measuring cup) — if Mars won't move on that item, the savings evaporate and the negotiation delivers little.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to close the 8.6% gap on the measuring-cup SKU — Premier Plastic delivers it at ₹0.35, and we're ready to talk faster payment in return for better pricing across the board.
